rule: owner_approved is false for every source: no outlet or provider has been approved by the owner. 'reviewed' means Claude read it for a specific claim on the date shown. Wire and news text is paraphrased, never reproduced; at most one short attributed quote per piece.

sources.name: Florida Division of Elections
sources.fetch_method: HTTP GET of CanList pages, stored with sha256 (tools/elections/fetch_fl_roster.py)
sources.redistribution: facts may be republished with attribution
sources.limits: 'Qualified' filter omits 'Unopposed'; statuses change on withdrawal

sources.name: Florida Legislature EDR, plan EOGPCRP2026
sources.redistribution: derived SVG paths published with attribution
sources.limits: county shares use Census cb_2024 county boundaries

sources.name: FEC (OpenFEC API)
sources.use: candidate totals, Schedule E independent expenditures
sources.fetch_method: API with FEC_API_KEY from the environment; never stored
sources.redistribution: allowed; FEC restricts using contributor data for solicitation
sources.limits: 24/48-hour notices and periodic reports overlap (dedupe in tools/dark_horse/schedule_e.py); by-candidate aggregates cover periodic filings only; direct PAC contributions (Schedule B) are deliberately NOT collected: the file is dominated by earmarked individual donations passed through the PAC and is not worth the pull; AIPAC ties come from news searches instead

sources.name: Kalshi public API v2
sources.use: contract quotes for House, Senate and governor party-winner markets
sources.fetch_method: unauthenticated GET; one attempt, no retry on 429
sources.license: venue terms not reviewed for raw republication
sources.redistribution: publish derived facts (ticker, bid, ask, last, time) with attribution; no raw feed mirror
sources.limits: party-winner contracts; no last-trade timestamp on the event payload

sources.name: Polymarket (Gamma and CLOB APIs)
sources.use: individual-winner contract quotes where an instrument is verified
sources.limits: only CA-14 and CA-11 individual contracts matched; none for Florida

sources.name: VoteHub polls API (beta)
sources.use: race-level poll discovery with original URL and sponsor
sources.license: UNVERIFIED: terms page returned HTTP 403 on 2026-10-23
sources.redistribution: facts stored with attribution; republish a poll only after the originator's release is checked
sources.limits: MOE, mode and release date absent; originals not reviewed

sources.name: 270toWin
sources.limits: discovery only until rights are clarified

sources.name: Pollsters' own releases (UNF PORL, St. Pete Polls, Change Research, Quantus, MDW and others)
sources.use: the only acceptable basis for a published poll figure
sources.fetch_method: open the release linked from the VoteHub row
sources.redistribution: cite pollster, sponsor, population, N, field dates, method, MOE
sources.limits: none opened yet except through news reports

sources.name: The Issues Party database (Supabase)
sources.use: profiles, race entries, six issue grades
sources.fetch_method: read-only export (scripts/export/state-packet.mjs) with the service key from .env.local, never copied
sources.limits: grades appear only on the profile that holds them; races.display_phase is stale and unused

sources.name: Reviewed news outlets (WLRN, WUSF and News Service of Florida, Newsweek, Reuters via GV Wire, Ballotpedia, AP via WTOP)
sources.fetch_method: WebFetch or search summary; the status is recorded per source
sources.limits: 'search_summary_only' sources are not usable until opened

sources.name: Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons
sources.use: secondary background; portraits and hero images with license on file
sources.fetch_method: API; a portrait is accepted only if the matched page title contains the candidate's first and last name
sources.license: per file (public domain, CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA)
sources.limits: secondary source for facts; never the sole basis for a vote count

sources.name: YouTube pages of campaigns and news outlets (metadata, captions, thumbnails only)
sources.use: find footage, read upload date, uploader, duration and license flag; caption text for timing
sources.fetch_method: yt-dlp --skip-download and oEmbed; no video downloaded unless the page carries a Creative Commons flag or written permission exists
sources.license: YouTube standard license unless the page shows Creative Commons; each upload belongs to its publisher
sources.redistribution: none without written permission; thumbnails and captions are internal reference only
sources.limits: captions are auto-generated and do not name speakers; yt-dlp may be rate-limited (HTTP 429)

sources.name: Florida Division of Elections, Election Watch (floridaelectionwatch.gov)
sources.use: statewide and county primary results (Aug 18, 2026 Democratic Senate: Nixon 705,835, Vindman 553,138)
sources.fetch_method: HTTP GET of /FederalOffices/USSenator and /ContestResultsByCounty/120002 (tools/video/fetch_florida_infographic_data.py; sha256 in infographics/data/sources.json)
sources.redistribution: facts may be republished with attribution
sources.limits: page is headed 'Official Election Results'; certification status not read; layout may change

sources.name: U.S. Census Bureau cartographic boundary file cb_2024_us_county_500k
sources.use: county outlines for the Florida county map

sources.name: Wikimedia Commons video and photo files (license per file)
sources.use: candidate photos and any video with a license on the file page
sources.license: per file; a tag that mirrors a YouTube upload is only as good as the original producer's right to license it
sources.limits: a public-domain tag on a politician's own branded edit is EDITORIAL_REVIEW, not CLEARED (the Moody HSGAC file)

sources.name: OpenFEC candidate totals (DEMO_KEY, read-only spot check)
sources.use: cross-check that a primary-time fundraising comparison is time-bound
sources.limits: cycle totals moved after the primary (Nixon $11.3M through Oct 14; Vindman $20.5M through Sep 30), so a '$16M vs under $1M' line is only true at the primary and must say so

sources.name: Washington Post analysis of the Aug 18 primary, read through a DNYUZ repost (Aug 19, 2026)
sources.use: attributed statement that Nixon's win was strongest in lower-income, less-college-educated and heavily Black counties; Nixon raised just under $1 million and Vindman $16 million (as of the primary)
sources.limits: original Post URL and byline not read; ATTRIBUTED only
